title: Raft-style follower for replicated match state
name: Match state replica

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this replica decides whether to accept entries from a leader? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The local log has entries at indexes 1-5 (terms 1,1,2,2,2). A request arrives with prevLogIndex 3, prevLogTerm 2, and one entry {index 4, term 3}. What is the log afterwards?
choices: Indexes 1-6 with the new entry appended at the end

questions.prompt: Why does commitIndex use Math.min(req.leaderCommit, lastNew) rather than just leaderCommit?
choices: To avoid applying entries the leader has not committed
Because this replica only knows its log matches the leader's up to lastNew; entries beyond that may be stale or missing
To slow down application under load
Because leaderCommit is always larger than the log length

questions.prompt: storage.save throws (disk full) partway through handleAppend after new entries were pushed. What does the caller observe and what state is left in memory?
choices: A success response, with the entries in memory but not on disk
The promise rejects; the in-memory log already contains the new entries, but commitIndex has not been advanced by this call
The promise rejects and the in-memory log is rolled back
